value.hook: When several mutant tests are expected to fail and shared-build --then stops at the first nonzero result
value.title: Batch expected mutant failures without restarting shared builds

sections.name: body
sections.value:
For expected-failure mutation batches, one Cargo test --no-fail-fast can collect selected targets across packages while retaining the shared-build lock. This avoids a fresh build per mutant and avoids losing later evidence when --then stops on the first failure.

Verified in the isolated #322 R2 archive:
just shared-build -- test --no-fail-fast -p pij-store -p pij-daemon --lib --test pr322_review review_mutant -- --nocapture

pr322_review was a review-owned integration target: recreate the isolated fixture and run from its manifest source tree, not an arbitrary checkout. Keep the canonical shared target, nice19 and four jobs.

The batch returned101 but ran all four mutants: three daemon failures and one store failure, each on its intended assertion. Sixty-three default controls passed separately. Exit101 alone is neither a product block nor mutation proof: verify test counts, actual oracle failures, no accidental infrastructure errors, and positive controls. A filter matching zero cases proves nothing.

Magic wand: retain per-case control/mutant results in the receipt rather than treating the overall command exit as the verdict.
